extracted.intended_audience: Members, officers, and administrators of the District of Columbia Bar (Board of Governors, Executive Committee, Nominations Committee, and general Bar membership)
extracted.subtask_short: D.C. Bar bylaws and membership rules
extracted.subtask_description: Official bylaws, membership manual provisions, and proposed rule amendments governing D.C. Bar governance, meetings, elections, committees, officer duties, membership classes, fees, reinstatement, indemnification, and related administrative procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Board meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonable written notice of the time, place, and if applicable, technology platform of such meetings, as well as subjects to be covered, shall be provided to all members of the Board and all required parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to regular and special meetings; 'reasonable' is the standard. Notice must include technology platform if meeting is electronic, and subjects to be covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition of unspecified matters at special meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any transactional business that is within the power of the Board may be conducted during a special meeting whether specified in the meeting notice or not provided two-thirds of the voting members of the Board present and voting approve the addition of the unspecified matter to the agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires two-thirds approval of voting members present and voting at the special meeting to add matters not listed in notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic meetings requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Board meetings may be held in person or electronically, as long as all attendees can simultaneously hear each other and participate during the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The President, the Board of Governors, or the Executive Committee shall determine whether to hold a meeting electronically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic attendance at meetings (Board members)
rubrics_metrics.description: Board members may, subject to the President’s discretion, participate in an in-person meeting electronically or other means by which all attendees can simultaneously hear each other and participate during the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation electronically is discretionary by the President; the technological condition is simultaneous hearing and participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board quorum
rubrics_metrics.description: A majority of the voting members of the Board shall constitute a quorum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A majority of voting members is required for the Board to transact business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting — no proxy and presence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be no proxy voting allowed. Voting members of the Board must be in attendance, in person or electronically, at the meeting at the time a vote is taken for their vote to count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action by a majority of the members present and voting shall constitute action by the Board. All votes shall be recorded in writing by the Secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action in lieu of a meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may take an official action in between regular meetings when the President, the Board of Governors, or the Executive Committee determines that such an action is necessary prior to the next regular meeting, and also determines that calling a special meeting is either not feasible or unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed action shall be presented to the Board in writing, a time limit for voting specified, and voting shall take place as prescribed in that writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Committee shall consist of the President, the President-Elect, the Immediate Past President, and four additional Board members annually appointed by the President and approved by the Board of Governors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointments of the four additional members are annual and subject to Board of Governors approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee meetings & quorum
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Committee shall meet at the call of the President, or upon call of the Secretary upon written application of three members of the Committee, upon one day’s notice. Five members shall constitute a quorum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action by a majority of the members present and voting at a meeting shall constitute action by the Committee. Members may participate electronically subject to President’s discretion. The President shall preside.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minutes of Executive Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Minutes of each meeting of the Executive Committee shall be taken and distributed to the members of the Board of Governors within a reasonable period following such meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minutes of the Committee shall be part of the permanent records of the Board of Governors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee powers and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Committee may exercise all the powers and perform all the duties of the Board of Governors between meetings of the Board, but only to the extent that action taken is not contrary to the instructions of the Board of Governors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Executive Committee shall not amend the Bylaws, make rules or regulations governing nominations or elections, or initiate the taking of any referendum or poll of members of the Bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officers — offices established
rubrics_metrics.description: The officers of the Bar shall be a President, a President-Elect, a Secretary, and a Treasurer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the enumerated officer positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officer qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Only Active members of the Bar shall serve as officers of the Bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officers must be Active class members in good standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of Secretary
rubrics_metrics.description: The President, at the beginning of the fiscal year, shall appoint a voting member of the Board of Governors to serve as a Secretary, subject to the approval of the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary appointment occurs at beginning of fiscal year and requires Board approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officer terms and term limits (Secretary)
rubrics_metrics.description: The officers shall serve for one year or until their successors are appointed or elected, and their term of office shall begin at the start of the fiscal year; provided however that the Secretary shall serve no more than three consecutive years in that office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General one-year terms; Secretary has a specific consecutive-year limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: General duties and compensation of officers
rubrics_metrics.description: The officers shall perform the following duties in addition to any other duties that may be prescribed under the authority of these Bylaws, other governing documents, and by the parliamentary authority adopted by the Bar. Officers may assign certain administrative duties of their office to be carried out by the Chief Executive Officer or their designee. Officers shall receive no compensation for their services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officers may delegate administrative tasks to the CEO/designee but are unpaid.

rubrics_metrics.name: President duties and continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: The President shall preside at all meetings of the Bar and of the Board of Governors, shall be an ex-officio member of all committees unless otherwise provided in these Bylaws, and shall remain on the Board as the Immediate Past President for the fiscal year following their year of service as President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: President has presiding and ex-officio roles and continues as Immediate Past President for one fiscal year after term.

rubrics_metrics.name: President-Elect duties and succession
rubrics_metrics.description: The President-Elect shall perform the duties of the President during any absence or temporary disability of the President, be an ex-officio member of all committees unless otherwise provided in these Bylaws and succeed to the office of President at the start of the fiscal year following their year as President-Elect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: President-Elect acts in President's absence and automatically succeeds to President next fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary shall be the legal custodian of the records of the Bar and take the minutes of the proceedings of the meetings of the Bar and of the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary is responsible for custody of records and minute-taking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treasurer duties and mentoring role
rubrics_metrics.description: The Treasurer shall keep correct and complete records of account showing accurately at all times the financial condition of the Bar; furnish, at meetings of the Board, or whenever requested, a statement of the financial condition of the Bar; and be the legal custodian of all moneys, notes, securities, and other valuables that may from time to time come into the possession of the Bar. The Treasurer shall also work with the Treasurer-Elect to help prepare them for their year as Treasurer. The Treasurer shall remain on the Board as an at-large member for the fiscal year following their year of service as Treasurer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treasurer has accounting, reporting, custody responsibilities and a mentorship/transition role with Treasurer-Elect and a one-year continued Board role after term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officer vacancies — President and President-Elect succession
rubrics_metrics.description: If a vacancy occurs in the office of the President, the President-Elect shall succeed to the office of the President and serve the remainder of the term of the President and, subsequently, the presidential term for which the President-Elect was elected. If a vacancy occurs in the office of the President-Elect, the Board shall elect one of its voting members to assume the duties of President-Elect for the remainder of the term. In the event of such vacancy, at the next Bar election, there shall be an election for the offices of President-Elect and President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate succession by President-Elect; Board fills President-Elect vacancies from voting members; next election includes both offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officer vacancies — Treasurer and Treasurer-Elect succession
rubrics_metrics.description: If a vacancy occurs in the office of the Treasurer, the Treasurer-Elect shall succeed to the office of the Treasurer and serve the remainder of the term of the Treasurer and, subsequently, the Treasurer term for which the Treasurer-Elect was elected. If a vacancy occurs in the office of the Treasurer-Elect, the Board shall elect one of its voting members to assume the duties of Treasurer-Elect for the remainder of the term. In the event of such vacancy, at the next Bar election, there shall be an election for the offices of Treasurer-Elect and Treasurer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treasurer-Elect succeeds to Treasurer; Board fills Treasurer-Elect vacancies; next election addresses both offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officer vacancy — Secretary
rubrics_metrics.description: If a vacancy occurs in the office of the Secretary, the President shall appoint a voting member of the Board of Governors to fill the vacancy, subject to the approval of the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: President-appointed, Board-approved replacement for Secretary vacancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: ABA Delegates representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The President and President-Elect shall serve as Delegates to the House of Delegates of the American Bar Association. At the close of the President’s term, the President shall continue in their office of President only to fulfill their service as Delegate if so required by the American Bar Association until the close of the ABA Annual Meeting in that calendar year. In the event that the President or President-Elect is unable to attend a meeting of the House of Delegates or is serving as a Delegate by reason of another election or appointment, the President shall, subject to Board approval, appoint an active member of the Bar to fill the vacancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: President/President-Elect automatically serve as ABA Delegates; temporary continuation in office solely to fulfill ABA delegate duties; Board approval required for appointees if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominations Committee composition and term limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The President, with the approval of the Board, shall appoint a Nominations Committee for a one-year term. The Nominations Committee shall consist of eight Active members of the Bar who are not members of the Board and the Immediate Past President who shall serve as an ex officio member. The President and President-Elect shall not serve as members of the Nominations Committee. Active members appointed by the Board shall serve on the Nominations Committee for no more than two consecutive terms. Members having served on the Nominations Committee in a fiscal year shall not be eligible to be nominated for any position on the ballot for the election in that same fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composition excludes Board members (except Immediate Past President ex officio) and the President/President-Elect; two-consecutive-term limit for committee appointees; service on committee precludes candidacy that fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of the Nominations Committee — slate delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nominations Committee shall prepare a list of eligible candidates for voting positions on the Board of Governors, to be elected by eligible D.C. Bar members. The Nominations Committee shall deliver its slate of candidates to the Secretary in accordance with a schedule determined by the Board or the Executive Committee. The Nominations Committee shall also deliver a list of eligible candidates for the three non-voting positions of the Board of Governors to be elected by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slate delivery follows schedule set by Board or Executive Committee; includes both member-elected and Board-elected (non-voting) positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominations — numeric slates for specific offices
rubrics_metrics.description: President-Elect: The Nominations Committee shall nominate at least two but no more than three Active D.C. Bar members for the office of President-Elect. Treasurer-Elect: The Nominations Committee shall nominate at least two but no more than three Active D.C. Bar members for the seat of Treasurer-Elect. Board of Governors: The Nominations Committee shall nominate at least two but no more than three Active D.C. Bar members for each Board vacancy to be filled in the subsequent election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum and maximum numbers specified for each slot ensure competitive slates while limiting choices to 2-3 nominees per position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominations for ABA Delegates — numeric and special-slot requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nominations Committee shall nominate at least one more nominee than the total number of vacancies to be filled but not more than two eligible D.C. Bar members for each vacancy as delegates to the American Bar Association to be filled at the ensuing election. Additionally, the Nominations Committee shall nominate at least two but no more than three eligible D.C Bar members, to comply with ABA delegate requirements for one elected delegate to be admitted to practice in their first bar within the past five years, or who must be less than 36 years old at the beginning of their term. Eligible nominees shall be separately slotted on the ballot and shall run against each other for one delegate position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides both over-nomination (one more than vacancies) and separate candidate slot(s) to meet ABA diversity/eligibility requirements (new admittee or under-36 delegate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominations by petition — signature threshold and filing deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for the offices of the President and the President-Elect, nominations may be made by a written petition that has been signed by at least one-half of one percent (0.5%) of the Active members of the Bar, based on the census of the Bar as of the first business day of the calendar year in which the petition is submitted. Nominating petitions shall be filed with the Secretary no later than 14 calendar days after the announcement of nominations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must be on the official form and comply with Board-established procedures. At minimum, petitions must contain legible handwritten eligible member signatures accompanied by the member’s license number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifying Bar members of nominations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary shall, no later than five business days after receiving the slate from the Nominations Committee, announce the list of the nominations for the ensuing election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely public announcement by Secretary is required within five business days of slate receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting method
rubrics_metrics.description: Voting shall be by secret ballot. Ballots shall contain the names of all nominees, in random order, for the respective positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Randomization prevents ordering bias; secret ballot preserves confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting eligibility cutoff
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible voters shall include all Active members in good standing as of the close of business on the second Monday in April.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voter eligibility is fixed by status on a specific date (second Monday in April).

rubrics_metrics.name: Election returns, certification, and challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: The President shall be present when the voting results are received and shall certify the voting results. The President shall preside over challenges made to the elections process and may exercise the discretion to elevate any such challenge to the Board whose decision shall be final. The candidates receiving the highest number of votes for their respective offices shall be declared duly elected. The certified voting results shall be published by the Bar on its website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: President has custody/certification role and gatekeeping authority on election challenges; Board decision is final on elevated challenges; results must be published online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board committees — scope and delegation limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may form standing committees and may delegate to such committees any of its powers, except the power to (a) elect or remove Board members or Board committee members; (b) approve the dissolution, merger or reorganization of the Bar or its affiliated entities, or distribution of the Bar’s assets or that of its affiliated entities; (c) amend the Bylaws; or (d) any such other matters as the Board may determine by a majority vote of the voting members of the Board. Any committee to which powers of the Board are delegated shall consist solely of members of the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation cannot include certain core governance powers; committees with delegated powers must be composed only of Board members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee quorums and voting
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided in a particular committee’s Board-approved governance document, a quorum of any committee shall be a majority of the members of the committee. Action of any committee shall be by majority vote of the members of the committee present and voting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default committee quorum is majority; default decision rule is majority of those present and voting unless committee document states otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee composition, duties, and service
rubrics_metrics.description: The composition of all committees, as well as the duties and terms shall be subject to Board approval. Committee members shall serve at the pleasure of the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board retains ultimate control over committee makeup, duties, and member tenure (may remove or replace members).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing Board committees and specific responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Standing Board Committees shall include the Audit Committee, Budget Committee, and Finance Committee. The Audit Committee shall provide independent oversight of the Bar’s financial reporting, internal controls and audit functions; and in so doing, shall have the authority to retain and discharge independent auditors to perform an annual audit and present their findings and recommendations to the Board. The Immediate Past President and Treasurer shall not serve on the Audit Committee. The Budget Committee shall oversee the preparation of an annual proposed budget which it recommends to the Board for approval. The President-Elect shall serve as the Chair of the Budget Committee. The Finance Committee shall oversee the Bar’s financial matters by monitoring, reviewing and reporting on the Bar’s financial and investment operations. The Finance Committee shall select the Bar’s investment advisors and determine whether to take action on the advisors’ recommendations. The Immediate Past President shall serve as the Chair of the Finance Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies roles, chair assignments, and membership exclusions to ensure independence and oversight in financial governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chief Executive Officer appointment and role
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chief Executive Officer ('CEO') shall be appointed by and serve at the pleasure of the Board. The CEO shall have general and active control over the Bar’s operations and personnel, be responsible for the administration of the Bar’s finances, and perform other duties incident to a chief executive officer of an organization that are not inconsistent with applicable law, the Rules, or these Bylaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEO is the Bar's administrative head subject to Board oversight; must act consistently with applicable laws and Bar governing documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parliamentary authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules contained in the latest edition of Robert’s Rules of Order Newly Revised shall govern the Bar in all cases to which they are applicable and in which they are not inconsistent with the Rules, these Bylaws, the Membership Manual, or any special rules of order of the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robert's Rules is the default parliamentary authority unless inconsistent with higher Bar rules/documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of Bylaws
rubrics_metrics.description: These Bylaws may be amended at any regular or special meeting of the Board by a two-thirds vote of the members of the Board of Governors present and voting, provided that notice of the amendment has been submitted in writing to the Board with the agenda of the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-thirds of those present and voting required and written notice of the proposed amendment must accompany the meeting agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory indemnification — eligibility conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bar shall indemnify any person who was or is a party or is threatened to be made a party to any action, suit or proceeding ... because he or she is or was an officer of the Bar, a member of the Board of Governors, an elected or appointed official of a Community, a member of a Committee of the Bar, a member of the Board on Professional Responsibility or its hearing committees or a monitor ... under the following circumstances: (1) where they have been successful on the merits or otherwise in defense of any such action, suit or proceeding, and (2) where they have settled the action or been unsuccessful on the merits and neither the Board nor an appropriate court has determined that the expenses have resulted from fraud, corruption, actual malice, or intentional wrongdoing on the part of the person claiming indemnification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indemnification covers expenses (including attorney's fees) actually and necessarily incurred in defense and/or good faith settlement; exclusions apply if wrongdoing (fraud, corruption, actual malice, intentional wrongdoing) is determined by Board or court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization and conditions for indemnification
rubrics_metrics.description: Any indemnification under paragraph (a) shall be made by the District of Columbia Bar only as authorized in the specific case by the Board upon its determination that indemnification is appropriate. The Board shall make determination and authorization by a majority vote of a quorum consisting of disinterested members. The Board shall have the right, as a condition of granting indemnification, to approve in advance the choice of counsel as well as any settlement by the person requesting indemnification. The Board shall not unreasonably withhold its approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indemnification requires Board authorization by disinterested majority; Board may condition indemnification on counsel/settlement approval but must not unreasonably withhold approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancing expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: When an action covered by Section 11.01 is pending or threatened, the District of Columbia Bar shall advance expenses (including reasonable attorney's fees) incurred by a person eligible for indemnification, upon (a) such terms and conditions as the Board, by a majority vote of a quorum of disinterested members, deems appropriate and (b) receipt of a promise by such person to repay such advances if it shall ultimately be determined that he or she is not entitled to be indemnified by the Bar as authorized under this Article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advances are discretionary and conditional on board-determined terms and a promise to repay if indemnification is later disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-exclusivity of indemnification
rubrics_metrics.description: The indemnification provided by this Article shall not be deemed exclusive of any other rights to which any person seeking indemnification may be entitled under any Bylaw, agreement, vote of the Board or members of the Bar, or otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other indemnity rights (contractual or statutory) remain available in addition to Article XI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insurance for officers and covered persons
rubrics_metrics.description: The District of Columbia Bar may purchase and maintain insurance on behalf of any person who is or was an officer of the Bar, a member of the Board of Governors, ... a paid employee of the Bar ... against any liability asserted against them and incurred by them in any such capacity or arising out of their status as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insurance is permissive (may purchase) to protect covered persons from liabilities arising from service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiscal year definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fiscal Year of the D.C. Bar shall begin on July 1st and end on June 30th of the following calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for officer terms, budget cycles, and other fiscal scheduling references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of bylaws revision (provisos)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided, That this revision shall become effective on July 1, 2022. Provided, That during fiscal year 2022-23, the Nominations Committee shall nominate at least two but no more than three Active D.C. Bar members for (a) the office of Treasurer and (b) the seat of Treasurer-Elect for service during fiscal year 2023-24. Provided, That during fiscal year 2023-23, there shall be an election for both the office of Treasurer and the seat of Treasurer-Elect for service during fiscal year 2023-24. The winner of the election for Treasurer shall serve a two-year term as follows (i) as Treasurer in their first year and (ii) as a non-voting member of the Board in their second year. The winner of the election for Treasurer-Elect shall serve a three-year term as follows: (i) as Treasurer-Elect in their first year; (ii) as Treasurer in their second year; and (iii) as a member of the Board in their third year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary transitional provisions specify nomination/election/term structures for Treasurer/Treasurer-Elect across fiscal years 2022-24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership Manual authority and amendment procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3.01 of the D.C. Bar Bylaws provides that the provisions and requirements contained in the D.C. Bar Membership Manual shall have the same weight and authority of these Bylaws. The Membership Manual shall be amended upon the recommendation of the Chief Executive Officer of the D.C. Bar and shall take effect unless the Executive Committee raises a written objection to the recommendation no later than two weeks after receiving written notice of such amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership Manual is binding like Bylaws and its amendments take effect automatically unless Executive Committee timely objects in writing within two weeks.

rubrics_metrics.name: License fee timing for new admittees
rubrics_metrics.description: Newly admitted members will be invoiced for the annual license fee the same month in which they are admitted. All annual license fees are due within 30 days of the invoice date. Persons who are sworn into the Bar between July 1 and December 31 shall pay the full amount of the annual license fee. Persons who are sworn in between January 1 and April 30 shall pay one-half the amount of the annual license fee. Any person who is sworn in after April 30 shall not be required to pay any license fees until the following annual license year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prorating rules for first-year license fees are calendar-period based; 30-day payment deadline applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late fees and administrative suspension for new admittees
rubrics_metrics.description: Newly admitted members of the Bar who have not paid the required annual license fee within 60 days of the original invoice date shall be assessed a late fee. Newly admitted members of the Bar who have not paid the required annual license fee and/or assessed fees associated with the invoice (including the late fee and/or returned payment fee) within 90 days of the original invoice date shall be automatically administratively suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 60 days triggers late fee; 90 days triggers automatic administrative suspension for nonpayment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of receipt for payments
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of receipt of the license fee and/or late fee shall be determined by the actual date of receipt of a payment. If payment is remitted by mail, delivery service or commercial carrier, the date of receipt shall be the postmark or ship date, as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mail/delivery postmark or ship date used to determine timely payment when mailed/carrier used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Course requirement for return-to-active
rubrics_metrics.description: Any admitted member of the Bar who has been Inactive or Retired, or has voluntarily resigned or been suspended for 5 years or more preceding a request to change their class of membership to Active or Retired, must complete the Mandatory Course even if they may have already previously completed the Course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory Course required if member held any status other than Active for the 5-year period immediately preceding the request to change to Active; applies to reactivations and some reinstatements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of membership class — fee adjustments and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Members who elect to change their class of membership to Active on or before December 31 shall be required to pay the full annual license fee due for the annual license year less the amount previously paid during that year. Members who elect to change their class of membership to Active after December 31 and before July 1 shall be required to pay one-half of the annual license fee for the annual license year less the amount previously paid during that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides formula for license fee adjustments when changing class to Active; members must use Bar-provided electronic means or other required methods to notify the Bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active to Inactive and Inactive to Active change procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Active class members in good standing may change their class of membership to that of Inactive by providing notice to the Bar through such means as the Bar provides electronically on its website or otherwise requires. Any Inactive class member in good standing may change their class of membership to that of Active class member by providing notice to the Bar through such means as the Bar provides electronically on its website or otherwise requires, requesting a transfer to the class of Active membership, and by paying the license fees required of Active class members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes of class require provision of notice via Bar-designated electronic or other procedures and payment when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial class ineligibility transition to Active
rubrics_metrics.description: Any judicial class member who is no longer a judge may change their class of membership to that of an Active member by providing notice to the Bar through such means as the Bar provides electronically on its website or otherwise requires, requesting a transfer to the class of Active membership and by paying the license fees required of Active class members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Former judges must follow notice and fee payment procedures to become Active members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired class eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A member in good standing who has retired from the practice of law (except, as provided in D.C. App R. 49, on a pro bono basis), or who is totally disabled and unable to practice law may elect the class of Retired membership by providing notice to the Bar ... Such member must certify that (a) they have been an Active class member of the Bar for five years (two years of any combination of Inactive or Judicial membership may be substituted for one year of Active membership to satisfy this requirement); and (b) they have been engaged in the practice of law in the District of Columbia or elsewhere for a combined total of 25 years. Retired members are required to provide the Bar with their contact information for the 5-year immediately following their becoming a Retired member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets active membership and practice-duration prerequisites for retirement classification and contact-info requirement for five years post-retirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resignation procedure and ODC consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member of the D.C. Bar who is in good standing, not under investigation pursuant to Rule XI, and who provides notice to the Bar ... of their election to discontinue the practice of law in the District of Columbia and to terminate their membership in the Bar, shall cease to be a member of the District of Columbia Bar only after consultation and approval by the Office of Disciplinary Counsel. This review process requires a minimum of 30 days during which time such member shall remain subject to all requirements of Bar membership and must remain in good standing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resignation requires ODC review/approval and a minimum 30-day review period during which membership obligations continue; resigning members must provide contact info for 5 years following resignation.

rubrics_metrics.name: General reinstatement approval by Office of Disciplinary Counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: All reinstatement requests must be approved by the Office of Disciplinary Counsel (ODC) in advance of a member’s reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is not effective until all conditions met and notice of approval is received from ODC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement after failure to file registration statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any admitted member of the Bar who fails to file a registration statement with the D.C. Bar may request reinstatement upon: (a) completion of the required reinstatement form provided on the Bar’s website; (b) submission of the registration statement; (c) payment of the required annual license fee for the annual license year of reinstatement; (d) payment of the required registration fee; and proof of completion of the Mandatory Course if such member was admitted after July 1, 1994, and has not yet completed the course, or such member was admitted before July 1, 1994, but has been suspended for five years or more and has not yet completed the course. Such registration shall be effective retroactively, as of the date of such original eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies forms, payments, and Mandatory Course evidence required for reinstatement for failure-to-register cases; reinstatement may be retroactive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement after failure to pay required annual license fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member who has been administratively suspended for failure to pay the required annual license fee may request reinstatement of membership upon: (a) completion of the required reinstatement form provided on the Bar’s website; (b) payment of the required annual license fee for the year of reinstatement; (c) payment of the required reinstatement fee; and (d) proof of completion of the Mandatory Course if such member was admitted after July 1, 1994, and has not yet completed the course, or such member was admitted before July 1, 1994, but has been suspended for five years or more and has not yet completed the course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement requires paperwork, payment(s), and potentially Mandatory Course completion depending on admission date and suspension duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement after failure to pay other fees (late/returned payment fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member who has been administratively suspended for failure to pay the required assessed late fee and/or returned payment fee shall be reinstated upon: (a) completion of the required reinstatement form provided on the Bar’s website; (b) payment of the required assessed late fee and/or returned payment fee by April 30th of the annual license year in which the suspension occurred; and (c) proof of completion of the Mandatory Course if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reinstatement request is received after April 30th of that year, follow procedures listed for failure-to-pay the annual license fee (E.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of newly admitted attorneys suspended for failure to complete Mandatory Course
rubrics_metrics.description: Newly admitted attorneys of the Bar suspended for failure to complete the Mandatory Course shall be reinstated upon: (a) completion of the required reinstatement form provided on the Bar’s website; (b) proof of completion of the Mandatory Course; (c) payment of any required outstanding license fee; and/or (d) payment of a reinstatement fee; and (e) submission of a statement that the member is not suspended, temporarily suspended, or disbarred by any disciplinary authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines proof of course completion, payments, declarations of disciplinary status, and form submission for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of Retired class members or resigned persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member who has elected the Retired class of membership or who has been approved to voluntarily resign their membership may request a change in their membership class or reinstatement to Active, Inactive, or Judicial membership upon: (a) completion of the required reinstatement form provided on the Bar’s website; (b) payment of the annual license fee for the current annual license year; (c) payment of a reinstatement fee; and (d) proof of completion of the Mandatory Course if such member was admitted after July 1, 1994 and has not yet completed the course, or such member has not been in the Active class of membership for five years or more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retirees/resignees must submit form, pay fees, and sometimes demonstrate Mandatory Course completion depending on time out of Active status or admission date.
